chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: "You Don't Know What Love Is" at the North Dallas Club
summary: Eckstine's slow ballad at a Dallas dance leads to a ruckus as dancers hold each other tightly.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So, and, anyway, Billy Eckstine got very popular, so I remember when we -- we had gone to Dallas,

Texas to play a dance up at the North Dallas Club. And, it -- the people were beginning to feeling good. They'd been drinking. You know how everybody have a ball at a dance. And, Billy was going to sing "You Don't Know What Love Is". And, I say -- I say, "Billy, I don't think it would be wise to sing that song right now. Let's wait till they change partners," I said, "because some of these guys' old ladies and, you know, and this was a slow, dreamy, beautiful number talking about love." I say, "All hell is liable to break loose out here with the cat grabbing its -- another cat's old lady up too tight and hugging and going on, and you know."
"Man, that's all right. We can play that." So, we started to playing this number. Billy started to sing, "And, You Don't Know What Love Is --"

And, these cats start -- they're getting all close and all hell broke loose in that ball room. Say -- I say, "Look it, you listen to me. This is my hometown. I know what happens when you do things like that, you know."
